<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`, `@objectstack/service-queue`, touching **13** documentable anchor(s).

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-handling-server.mdx`  _(via ScopedContext (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx`  _(via ScopedContext (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`  _(via MessagingServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via ScopedContext (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via MessagingServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx`  _(via MessagingServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via MessagingServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 82 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **54** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 247382446d968e3b39635ed416275581f09117f2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b9e8d9d8c077fba5f19c6f36d407919220445945` — the merge of head `62064b52334ae7f6452474523247b1469c32c392` into base `247382446d968e3b39635ed416275581f09117f2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b9e8d9d8c077fba5f19c6f36d407919220445945 && git checkout b9e8d9d8c077fba5f19c6f36d407919220445945
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 247382446d968e3b39635ed416275581f09117f2 62064b52334ae7f6452474523247b1469c32c392 && git checkout -B drift-repro 247382446d968e3b39635ed416275581f09117f2 && git merge --no-ff 62064b52334ae7f6452474523247b1469c32c392

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 247382446d968e3b39635ed416275581f09117f2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 247382446d968e3b39635ed416275581f09117f2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `dbe4ac7ac20b52bb48b36b1b5a96769a58cac8b5`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration (`Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and the changeset); no published schema and no governed path in the file list, so no ④. Inputs: card #37705 with every comment, this PR's body and 8-file net diff against `main` (merge-base `0f8e13b0`), and the head's check-runs (57 success, 13 skipped, 0 failed, none pending; all eleven required contexts green). The PR is still a draft.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`ObjectQL.runOutsideOpenUnits(body)` (new public member on an exported class): right.** It is a one-line delegate to the existing `runOutsideOpenUnits(txStore, undefined, body)` in `unit-detach.ts`: it leaves the engine's ambient unit entry and records that entry's handle as detached. No handle is threaded, which is correct here because the store's statements carry `SYSTEM_CTX` and no `transaction`. Nothing that is already accepted changes.
- **The detach matches the async-hook exit only for `afterFind`, not for the write events.** `engine-scoped-context.ts` sends a write event's `async` run through `runOutsideOpenUnitsOnCommit`: it waits for the unit's commit and is dropped on rollback (#33760). The new member starts at once and is never dropped. That is a deliberate choice, and the changeset and the docblock state it. F-1 grades the result.
- **`SuspendedRunStoreEngine.runOutsideOpenUnits?` (optional member on an exported type): right.** The registered `objectql` and `data` services are both the `ObjectQL` instance, so the shipped composition takes the detached arm. A double without units keeps the old in-place write. `recordTerminal` drops `async` but still returns `writeTerminal`'s promise, and its only caller (`run-history.ts`, `void write.catch`) never awaits it. So no single-connection pool can deadlock on a detached write that a caller is awaiting.
- **No write that must be atomic with the triggering write escapes.** Only the terminal history row (find, upsert, retention prune) is detached. The run's own node writes, the pause write and the suspension claim stay in the unit, awaited. Paused rows (raw `runId`) and terminal rows (`run_` + runId) are disjoint, so a detached upsert cannot race the unit's claim delete on the same row.
- **`DispatchLoop` ticks in its constructor's async context: right, and safe for context.** All four in-tree loops (notification, HTTP delivery, DB queue, audit sealer) are constructed at boot (constructor, `start()` from `kernel:ready`, or plugin start). None of their ticks reads an ambient store, because delivery rows carry their own tenant and recipient. Timer-driven ticks never had the waker's context anyway, so no delivery depended on it. `start()`, `wake()`, `wakeAt()` with a past due time, and a future `wakeAt()` timer are all re-homed. The `node:async_hooks` import matches the `node:crypto` and `node:net` imports already on core's main entry.
- **Root cause and coverage of the reproduction: right for the two producers measured.** The card's audit failures are the `sys_activity` rows that the notification tick's delivery updates fire. The PR measured 0 "Transaction query already complete" lines in hotcrm with the fix. F-4 names other candidates of the same class.
- **Tests: they fail without the fix, by reading.** objectql: with `return body()`, the detached read takes the unit's handle (`seen` equals `[begun[0]]`), and the inner `transaction()` joins the outer unit (`begun` length 1). Both cases go red and the CONTROL stays green. service-automation: without the routing, every statement records `outside: false`, so 2 cases go red. core: without `loopTickAtHome`, the tick sees the waker's store, so 2 cases go red. That matches the reported 6/6.
- **Read-after-write sweep: it holds for `sys_automation_run`.** Every listed reader of the durable row already waits with a bound (10 s, 100 × 20 ms, 50 × 100 ms) or reads the in-memory log. The unlisted readers I checked read rows that are not the terminal write of a run fired inside a unit: schedule-fired runs, restored-approval `hasSuspendedRun`, stubbed runtime doors. Test Core and Dogfood Regression are green on this head. The sweep's DispatchLoop sentence does not hold on every driver: see F-2.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/service-automation` and `@objectstack/core` at `patch`. The diff publishes one new public method, one new optional interface member and a tick-context change. It adds no authorable key, no accepted value and no metadata type, so `Metadata-protocol: none` is right, and under the level rule a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. The level is right.
- `Clause-②:` the PR body and the changeset each carry `Clause-②: yes (widening)` at the start of a line. That is right for a public member added to an exported class with no signature or input narrowed. The card's `Clause-②: no` was filed before the fix existed, and the PR correctly supersedes it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **F-1 · nit: the terminal row now outlives a rolled-back triggering write.** On a pooled driver it can also commit before that write is visible. A `completed` history row can therefore name a run whose in-unit effects were rolled back, and a `trigger_record_id` can name a row that is not yet visible. The changeset and the `unit-detach.ts` docblock declare this. It is defensible: a run whose failure caused the rollback must keep its row, which the commit-and-drop posture of #33760 would erase. Accepted as a deviation; nothing is owed in this PR.
- **F-2 · should-fix: a wake made inside a unit can no longer see the row it was woken for, on a pooled driver.** The woken tick now runs outside the unit, so on Postgres or MySQL it cannot see the outbox or queue row the uncommitted unit just enqueued, and `nextDueAt` cannot see it either. The tick finds nothing, and the row waits for the next backoff tick: twice `intervalMs` by default, and `maxIdleIntervalMs` (30 s by default) when `soleWriter` is set, whose premise is that wakes carry the work. On a single-connection pool, which is the hotcrm case, the tick waits for the connection and sees the committed row. So the sweep's sentence that `sys_activity` and delivery rows "land when they did" holds only there. Close this either way: (a) the wake fires on the unit's commit, which the producer that enqueues through the engine can arrange; or (b) correct the PR body and changeset to state the pooled-driver latency, and file it as a follow-up card under the filing gate.
- **F-3 · should-fix: the card is not delivered whole by `Fixes #37705`.** The card's acceptance also requires hotcrm's six lead_assignment tests to pass on the release that carries the fix, and that cannot be observed at merge. The PR body also says three hotcrm `case_escalation` reads, which passed on `main`, need the file's own bounded wait (`landedRuns`) because of this change. No card tracks either item. Before ACCEPT: file the hotcrm-side card for the three reads, and either switch to `Refs #37705` so the card stays open until the release check, or record on the card that the hotcrm card owns that check.
- **F-4 · nit: candidates of the same class, outside the diff.** `plugin-audit`'s read-audit and dataset-query-audit batchers are enqueued from a synchronous `afterFind` (`recordView`). The batcher calls `void runFlush()` at `maxBatchSize` and arms its flush timer in the reader's async context. A user-principal read inside an open unit can therefore start a `sys_audit_log` persist enrolled in that unit, which can then outlive it. This is unmeasured and needs a reproduction before a card (Prime Directive 10). The PR body already names `runOutsideOpenUnits` as the exit for the next such producer.
- **F-5 · nit: the loop's home is wherever it was constructed.** Every in-tree construction runs at boot. But `DbQueueAdapter.start()` is also reachable from `subscribe()` under `autoStart`, and a lazy first subscribe inside a request would make that request's context the loop's home for good. A sentence in the `DispatchLoop` docblock naming the boot-construction invariant would close this.
- **SQL push-down: no finding.** The diff adds no id materialisation and no in-app join. The in-app sort and per-row delete in `pruneFlowOverflow` predate the diff; it is only re-routed here.
- Dev flags and open questions: the PR body's two flags are answered above. The missing framework end-to-end twin is acceptable, because the engine pin holds the race by construction (the driver holds the read until after the commit). The hotcrm three-line change is F-3. The report carries no `open_questions` entry. The PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no author note is owed.
- Remaining before ACCEPT: close F-2 and F-3 (each a delta read by this reviewer), then take the PR out of draft.

Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `f94bcab7d35570caf826930c52a256f40efadaae`
Local-runs: none

This is the delta round on my round-1 record (7207454847, head `dbe4ac7ac2`). Face: declaration, as before. I read the delta `dbe4ac7ac2..f94bcab7d3` (2 commits, 10 files), the PR body as it now stands, card #37705, and the head's check-runs. Each round-1 finding is closed or kept below by id.

Gate line: **CI on this head is still running at review time.** 13 checks succeeded, 12 were skipped and 23 are in progress, including Test Core 1-10, Build Core, the Type Check and Lint lanes, and Live E2E UI. The one `cancelled` run is a superseded PR-body-guards run: a later run of the same name succeeded. None has failed yet. This record does not certify the gate. It has to be read green before ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`ObjectQL.runAfterOpenUnitsCommit(body)` (new public member): right.**
  - It queues `body` on the ambient unit's #33760 `UnitCommitQueue`, bound to the caller's async context. It runs outside every unit once `transaction()` settles the queue, which happens after `commit` returns.
  - It is dropped in the `catch` arm on any failure, whether a callback throw or a commit failure.
  - When no unsettled unit exists, it runs at once outside the units.
  - A nested `transaction()` joins the outer entry (ADR-0067 D2), so a wake made there waits for the outermost commit.
  - The write door's own unit (`inAfterAbortUnit`) is a `transaction()`, so it carries a queue. That is the reproduction's case.
- **Is a wake lost or stuck? No in-unit row loses its wake.**
  - On rollback, the enqueued row rolls back with the unit, so dropping its wake is correct.
  - A unit that never settles also never commits its row.
  - A run detached by `txStore.exit` finds no ambient unit and wakes at once.
  - The DispatchLoop's own timer stays the floor for every row: a missed wake costs one backoff interval, never the row. F-6 and F-7 cover the two residual edges.
  - A deferred `publish` keeps `wakeAt`, which now only arms a timer. If that timer fires while the publishing unit is still open, a pooled driver misses the row once and backs off. This is narrow and bounded, so it is not a finding.
- **Atomicity and errors.** The body runs after the commit and outside every unit, so nothing it does can be atomic with the write. The four wired bodies are bare `wake()` calls, which write nothing and throw nothing. See F-8 for the public contract's wording.
- **`wakeAfterOpenUnitsCommit(engine, wake)` (new root export of `@objectstack/core`): right.** It wakes through the engine when the engine has the member, and otherwise at once. In production the `engine` it receives is the `ObjectQL` instance in all four wirings: the notification outbox, the HTTP outbox (including `redeliverHttp`, which shares `onHttpDeliveryEnqueued`), the queue's due `publish`, and `replay`.
- **The `engine.ts` docblock compression is pure wording.** The `[DETACHED_HOOK_RUN]` comment merges two sentences into one, with the same claim. No code changed.
- **Pins: by reading, they fail without the wiring.**
  - objectql: 3 of 4 go red with an at-once implementation (the event order, the handle seen, a signal on rollback). The no-unit case is the control.
  - core: 1 goes red if the helper calls `wake()` directly. The member-absent case is the control.
  - service-queue: 2 go red without the wiring (`held` is empty for publish and for replay).
  - service-messaging: 1 goes red on the spy count. It runs on a real engine over SQLite, in a real `transaction()`.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset now names `@objectstack/service-messaging` and `@objectstack/service-queue` at `patch` beside objectql, service-automation and core. Those two change only when a wake is sent, so `patch` is right.
- The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` lines in the PR body and the changeset list the whole new public surface: two `ObjectQL` methods, the core root export, and the optional `SuspendedRunStoreEngine` member. The new `unit-detach.ts` function is not reachable from the objectql entry. `Metadata-protocol: none` still holds. The level is still right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **F-1 · nit:** kept as an accepted deviation, unchanged by the delta.
- **F-2 · should-fix: CLOSED.** Route (a) holds against the tree. The wake goes at the commit of the unit that wrote the row, on the same queue and at the same settle point #33760's async runs use, and not at all on rollback. The PR body's sweep sentence is corrected.
- **F-3 · should-fix: STILL OPEN.** The PR body still reads `Fixes #37705`. No hotcrm card is filed for the three `case_escalation` reads, and card #37705 carries no note on who owns its release-side acceptance check. The delta does not touch this.
- **F-4 · nit:** kept, unchanged. It is outside the diff and needs a reproduction before a card.
- **F-5 · nit: CLOSED.** The `DispatchLoop` docblock now states that a loop is built at boot, and names `DbQueueAdapter.start()` reached from `subscribe()` under `autoStart`. The changeset says the same.
- **AuditSealer item: CLOSED.** The audit-seal loop is now in the loop list in the PR body and the changeset.
- **F-6 · nit (new): the `ScopedContext` `beginTransaction`-trio gap is acceptable, and narrower than the PR declares.**
  - The PR body and the changeset say a trio unit "does not hold the wake back". The tree is better than that. While an engine call that carries the trio handle runs, `publishTrioHandleFor` publishes the handle into the ambient entry together with the trio's own queue (`trioCommitQueueOf`). `commitTransaction` and `rollbackTransaction` settle that queue (`settleTrioCommitQueue`).
  - So a wake made inside such a call, which is where an enqueue's `onEnqueued` runs, already waits for the trio's commit.
  - The gap left is a wake made outside any such call, by code that holds the trio handle only explicitly. It goes at once, as in round 1. On a pooled driver that costs one backoff interval, never the row.
  - Accepted. Optionally, narrow the declaration in the PR body and changeset to that case. The sweep's "on every driver" sentence should carry the same exception.
- **F-7 · nit (new): a dropped wake for a row that did commit.**
  - Case: the outbox or queue table sits on a datasource the open unit does not cover. Its insert then commits on its own connection, which the same-origin gate allows for system ledgers, while the wake still rides the unit's queue.
  - Consequence: on rollback the wake is dropped. The row goes out on the next backoff tick, at most `maxIdleIntervalMs`. No in-tree composition was measured that way.
- **F-8 · nit (new): the wording of `runAfterOpenUnitsCommit`'s public contract.**
  - The docblock says a throw from `body` after the commit "is the body's own". In fact `settleUnitCommitQueue` swallows a synchronous throw with no log, a rejected promise from an `async` body is unhandled, and on the no-unit path the throw reaches the caller.
  - Unlike its sibling `runOutsideOpenUnits`, it carries no ⛔ line against routing work that must be atomic with the write.
  - Fix: state both in the docblock. A wording change.
- **F-9 · should-fix (new): `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx:495-497` is now false inside a unit.**
  - The page says `messaging.enqueueHttp()` and `messaging.redeliverHttp()` wake the dispatcher "so a delivery written there goes out at once".
  - Against the tree: both call `onHttpDeliveryEnqueued` (`messaging-service.ts`), which the plugin now routes through `wakeAfterOpenUnitsCommit`. Inside a unit the delivery goes out at that unit's commit, and not at all on rollback. Outside a unit it goes at once.
  - The sentence needs that qualifier.
  - The other four hand-written pages docs-drift lists (`api/error-handling-server.mdx`, `automation/hook-bodies.mdx`, `permissions/system-context.mdx`, `plugins/packages.mdx`) name only `ScopedContext` or `MessagingServicePlugin` and state no wake timing. I spot-checked them: no edit is owed. The two release-owned pages are read-only.
- **Regression of round-1 closures: none.** The delta adds no write path. The terminal history row and its detach are unchanged, so the round-1 atomicity, deadlock and context judgments stand.
- **SQL push-down: no finding.** The delta adds no id materialisation and no in-app join.
- The PR is still a draft. Its author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no author note is owed.
- **Remaining before ACCEPT:**
  1. Close F-3.
  2. Close F-9.
  3. Read every check on this head green.
  4. Take the PR out of draft.
  The F-3 and F-9 fixes are a body, card and docs change, which this reviewer reads as a delta. F-6, F-7 and F-8 are nits that may ride along or be accepted.

Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `62064b52334ae7f6452474523247b1469c32c392`
Local-runs: none

This is delta round 3 on my round-2 record (7208126545, head `f94bcab7`). Face: declaration, as before.

I read four things:
- the delta `f94bcab7..62064b52`: one commit, 3 files;
- the PR body as it now stands;
- card #37705 with its new comment 7208160602, and objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2822;
- the check-runs on this head.

**Gate line: CI on this head is still running at review time.** 9 checks have succeeded, 11 were skipped and 21 are in progress, including Build Core, every Type Check and Lint lane, Check Changeset and Live E2E UI. Test Core and Test UI have not started.

The run on `f94bcab7` was cancelled when this head was pushed. Its two `failure` rows (`TypeScript Type Check`, `Test UI`) are the roll-up jobs over shards that were cancelled at 02:34Z, not measured failures. So no completed gate yet covers the code, which is unchanged since `f94bcab7`. This record does not certify the gate. Every check has to be read green before ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The delta is comment and docs only. That holds.**
  - It changes one sentence of the changeset prose and appends one sentence to `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`.
  - In `unit-detach.ts` it rewrites only the docblock above `runAfterOpenUnitsCommit`.
  - It touches no code line, no export, no test and no changeset frontmatter.
- **Each new sentence is true against the tree.**
  - **The webhooks.mdx sentence.** `enqueueHttp()` and `redeliverHttp()` both call `onHttpDeliveryEnqueued`, which the plugin routes through `wakeAfterOpenUnitsCommit`.
    - Inside a transaction the delivery goes out at that transaction's commit.
    - On rollback the row rolls back with the transaction and its wake is dropped.
    - Before the commit, a pooled driver's tick cannot see the row.
    - The one place the sentence over-reaches is the accepted F-7 composition: there the row commits on its own and goes out on a later tick. That is covered by F-7's acceptance and is not a new finding.
  - **The `runAfterOpenUnitsCommit` errors paragraph.**
    - With no unit open, the body runs synchronously inside `txStore.exit` and its throw reaches the caller.
    - At the commit, the `try/catch` in `settleUnitCommitQueue` discards a synchronous throw without logging it. That covers the trio's commit too, because `settleTrioCommitQueue` delegates to it.
    - A body typed `() => void` that returns a rejected promise is never observed, so the rejection is unhandled.
    - The new ⛔ line, never route atomic work through it, matches the fact that the body runs after the commit and outside every unit.
  - **The trio sentence** (docblock, changeset, PR body, sweep).
    - `publishTrioHandleFor` publishes the trio handle together with `trioCommitQueueOf(explicit)` while an engine call carrying it runs. So a wake made there waits for the trio's commit.
    - A wake made outside such a call goes at once.
    - This is now stated the same way in all four places.
- **No round-1 or round-2 judgment regresses.** No code moved, so ①'s judgments from round 2 stand: the commit-time wake, the detach of the run-history write, and the DispatchLoop's home context.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset frontmatter is unchanged: five packages at `patch`.
- The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` lines in the PR body and the changeset are unchanged, and so is `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- The level is still right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **F-1 · nit:** kept. It is an accepted deviation, now listed in the PR body's Acceptance notes.
